evidence: Gates: authenticated_render and server_backed_local_application are type=binary with all_pass (render/constraints judge.toml:20-24), matching staged-task-contract.md:96. Functional: all 16 criteria (signin_and_client_scope ... persistence) are type=binary, each a concrete pass/fail behaviour with explicit 'Fails if' conditions and positive controls; none grades degree of quality. Polish: 6 binary criteria (enter_sends, escape_closes, delete_confirm, link_highlight, transcript_print, refusal_in_place, polish/judge.toml:20-72) are discrete keyboard/confirm/highlight/overflow/refusal behaviours with explicit fail conditions, consistent with the template's binary polish dimension. Visual (craft): matter_sidebar, retention_marks, transcript_page, phone_chambers are type=likert, points=5 (visual/judge.toml:20-82), each with a described anchor at every level 5,4,3,2,1,0, exactly the shipped template format (template visual_typography etc. also use likert points=5 with 0-5 anchors); visual/prompt.md:28-36 states the anchored 0-5 scale is authoritative over RewardKit's generic 1-5 hint, also template text. Per SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170 the workbook internal note ('Likert we dont use') is a known false positive; judged against shipped format. Counterexample search: a weak app cannot gain partial binary credit for a half-working behaviour (binary is conjunctive), and a conforming app with mediocre-but-working craft gets graded gradation rather than a binary zero; matter_sidebar explicitly avoids penalising absent unread counts at look time, so a conforming alternative is not failed for state timing. No binary craft criterion and no likert block with missing anchors found. Static structural check; no runtime measurement is required for this row and none is claimed.
